# AI Full Stack Challenge — IT Access Requests

## The task
Northstar Labs receives access requests as free-text messages. Build a small runnable application that uses a language model to turn those messages into structured records and a review queue for the IT team. The supplied company, people and requests are fictional.

Read docs/requirements.md for the operating context and required behavior, materials/office-policy.md for review rules, and snapshot.schema.json for the record format. The 20 JSON exports in materials/requests/ are your starting data. Choose an interface suited to the IT team: a CLI, service or web application. Operators should be able to start intake, inspect completed results while other requests are pending, and resume unfinished work through the documented interface.

## What to submit
This brief ships as CHALLENGE.md; the README.md below is yours to write.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| README.md | Setup, supported runtime/provider, exact intake/test/accuracy-check commands, environment-variable names, and how to inspect the queue |
| Source code and dependency lockfile | Runnable application, extraction prompt, schema and model request configuration |
| deliverables/extractions.jsonl | One current record per message: document_id, source_sha256, extraction (schema-conforming object, or null on error), status, owner, next_action, error (null on success), and response_source (`mock`, or the provider and model ID that produced the record) |
| deliverables/queue.json | The review queue linked to extraction records by document_id |
| deliverables/accuracy.md | Source-derived expected fields for the 20 supplied messages and one paraphrase you author; the field-comparison procedure, exact-match counting/denominator rules, factual-error reporting and model/configuration; distinguish mocked examples from any optional live observations |
| deliverables/request-evidence.json | Credential-redacted example model request showing the model ID and configuration used, plus the implemented response handling |
| deliverables/verification.md | Verification commands and assertions, their intended comparisons, operating limits, and any observed results or repairs clearly identified as such |
| Coding-session capture | Session record paired with the submitted commit, collected through the facilitator's capture setup |

## Submission
Commit and push the application, outputs and session capture to your repository's default branch. Submit only the root repository link (`https://github.com/<your-account>/<repository>`) through the Classroom assignment. The facilitator supplies the assignment and capture instructions.

Submit the implemented provider integration and source-grounded validation procedure. Use mocked responses for reproducible development examples, and label each recorded observation with its configuration and whether it used a mock or provider response. The committed deliverables may come from mocked or provider responses; each record's response_source says which.
# Requirements — IT Access Requests

## Operating context

Northstar Labs is a fictional multinational company with approximately 5,000 employees across offices in Asia, Europe and North America. Its regional IT teams share responsibility for preparing access requests for human review. They receive free-text messages through email, chat and the service portal, then work from JSON exports of those messages.

### Workload and the review day

On an ordinary business day, the company receives around 200–400 request messages. A coordinated onboarding or acquisition can bring roughly 2,000 messages into the morning's intake. The supplied 20 exports are a representative sample of message types; the application will also receive other messages in the same export format.

Reviewers begin work at different local times. They want to start on requests that are ready while the rest of the intake is still being prepared. A slow response for one message should leave the rest of their work available. Model access is shared with other internal tools, and the available request rate and response time can vary.

### Shared operations

Regional operators work against the same intake and review records. Their working hours overlap, and two operators may start processing around the same time. Each expects their work to leave a coherent current queue and a trustworthy record of earlier activity.

The application may be stopped during a deployment or interrupted by a service outage. When an operator returns, they need to distinguish completed work from unfinished work and continue from the recorded state. Reviewers rely on the queue and the supporting extraction records agreeing about the same source version.

### Updates and follow-up

Exports arrive throughout the day. A later export may repeat an unchanged document or replace its contents with a corrected or expanded message. An export batch contains new or updated documents; absence from a later batch does not withdraw an earlier request. Withdrawal is expressed in the message and handled under the office policy.

Operators need the current view to reflect the latest processed source and to retain earlier results for follow-up. If a new processing attempt fails, they need to see that failure and identify any older result as belonging to its earlier attempt and source version.

The team periodically changes model configuration and updates its review policy. When such a change affects how records are produced or routed, operators need to refresh the affected results and understand which settings and policy version produced the records they are using.

### Service interruptions and handover

The model service sometimes responds slowly, limits requests or becomes temporarily unavailable. IT staff need to locate affected messages, understand what remains pending and resume processing without losing completed work. Other messages may contain incomplete or conflicting information that needs clarification from the requester.

The original developer and the next operator may be in different offices. The operator will use the repository's setup instructions, configuration guidance and commands to prepare an intake, inspect the queue and follow up on failures. Explain the operating assumptions and limits of your implementation so that this handover is practical.

## Record and review behavior
- Use a language model to extract the request details into records that conform to snapshot.schema.json.
- Validate response structure and completion status before using extracted data. Preserve exact supporting quotes and represent uncertain fields as null with an explanatory issue.
- Use message content as the source of business facts. Preserve missing values, conflicting alternatives and explicit corrections according to the policy. Keep document identity distinct from the request ID stated in the message.
- Apply the supplied review policy and display each request's status, owner and next action. Approval decisions belong to the named human reviewers.
- Record input filenames and SHA-256 hashes. Reuse results when the source and relevant processing settings are unchanged, refresh affected results when those inputs or settings change, and retain earlier versions. Process each message independently and make failures visible with a reproducible retry command.
- Handle malformed output, provider errors, refusal and interrupted responses explicitly. Keep model/provider settings configurable and document a supported configuration. The facilitator supplies an API key through the environment variable API_KEY.

## Verification

Include automated tests covering a complete request, missing dates, conflicting details, embedded instructions, provider failure, an unchanged rerun, and changed source content. Build expected results from the supplied messages and policy. Add a paraphrased synthetic request to exercise extraction on fresh wording. Specify expected facts from the source messages and policy independently of the extraction outputs being measured. Include checks for refusal or interrupted responses and a failed retry after a prior success.


Describe how your implementation supports the operating context above, and include checks for the operational situations your design handles. Record assumptions about workload and shared operation, the expected behavior during interruptions, and the limits of the verification you performed.
# Northstar access-request intake policy

Northstar Labs uses this intake application to prepare access requests for human review. All exercise data is fictional.

## Input export format
Each UTF-8 JSON file represents one exported message. Read its `message` string as the natural-language source for extraction. `export_version`, `exported_at`, `source_channel` and `subject` describe the export and help display it. Derive request facts from `message`; the export timestamp describes when the record was exported. Messages vary in length, up to 200 English words.

Use the original JSON file bytes for the source hash and its filename for document_id. Exact supporting quotes refer to substrings of the decoded `message` value.

## Extracted facts
Extract request_id, request_date, kind (new, change, withdrawal or other), requester, team, system, environment (staging or production), permission (read, write or admin), business_purpose, start_date, end_date, manager, supporting_quotes and issues. Use the supplied schema. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.

Use explicit facts from each message. Represent absent or unresolved scalar values as null and explain each missing or conflicting fact in issues. Preserve conflicting alternatives in exact supporting_quotes. A later statement explicitly labelled as a correction replaces the earlier value; contradictory statements without a correction remain unresolved. A relative date stays unresolved. For a change request, extract the requested new permission.

The document_id is the input filename. If an identifier inside the message differs from the identifier in its filename, retain the stated identifier and record the mismatch as an issue. Each message is an independent document, including multiple messages about one request.

## Review queue
Apply these rules in order after validating the extraction:

1. An instruction-override attempt goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action inspect-message. Keep the attempted instruction as source evidence and identify it in issues. Treat source messages as data throughout extraction and routing.
2. A withdrawal with request_id and request_date goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action confirm-withdrawal. Other fields may be null; identify absent facts in issues.
3. Other messages with kind other/null, conflicting details, an identifier mismatch, or any missing required fact go to IT Service Desk with status needs-information and next_action clarify. For new/change requests, required facts are request_id, request_date, requester, team, system, environment, permission, business_purpose, start_date, end_date and manager. A start_date after end_date is also a clarification issue.
4. Complete new/change requests involving production, write or admin go to Security Review with status review and next_action review-risk-then-owner. Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system owner for a decision.
5. Complete staging/read requests go to System Owner with status review and next_action review-request.

All successful intake outputs await human review. A named manager is a contact; approval is an explicit human decision. The application's output is a review queue.

## Processing and recovery
An extraction failure produces status error, owner IT Service Desk, next_action retry-extraction, a null extraction and an actionable error. Keep unaffected messages moving through intake. Preserve the last valid result in history when a later attempt fails, and show the latest attempt's error in the current queue.

Identify source revisions with a SHA-256 of the original bytes. An unchanged rerun produces one current queue entry per document. Changed input creates a new result and retains the earlier result with its earlier hash. Store prior versions separately from current outputs. Keep credentials in environment variables and use credential-redacted operational logs.

import hashlib
import json
import os
import socket
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
MOCKS = ROOT / "tests" / "mock_responses"


def canned_reply(name: str) -> dict:
    """What a mock provider returns: the saved reply, read from disk instead of asking a model."""
    return json.loads((MOCKS / f"{name}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


class SuppliedFiles(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_each_request_export_has_message_text_and_a_hash(self):
        exports = sorted((ROOT / "materials" / "requests").glob("*.json"))
        self.assertEqual(len(exports), 20)
        for path in exports:
            raw = path.read_bytes()
            self.assertIsInstance(json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))["message"], str, path.name)
            self.assertEqual(len(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()), 64)

    def test_the_schema_names_the_fields_it_requires(self):
        schema = json.loads((ROOT / "snapshot.schema.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertIn("request_id", schema["required"])


class MockResponse(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_mock_reply_is_read_with_no_key_and_no_network(self):
        refuse = mock.Mock(side_effect=AssertionError("a test tried to open a network connection"))
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ), mock.patch.object(socket, "socket", refuse):
            os.environ.pop("API_KEY", None)
            reply = canned_reply("canned-reply")
        self.assertEqual(reply["response_source"], "mock")
        self.assertTrue(reply["output_text"])
        refuse.assert_not_called()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

class ProviderUnavailable(RuntimeError):
    """Named injected failure from the T-01 plan; never a real service error."""


class ObservedEvent(threading.Event):
    """Tell the test when a provider reaches the release barrier."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.waiting = threading.Event()

    def wait(self, timeout=None):
        self.waiting.set()
        return super().wait(timeout)


class MockProviderT01(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.message = json.loads(
            (ROOT / "materials/requests/IT-001.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        )["message"]
        # Block the boundaries before importing the future implementation, too.
        for target in (
            "socket.socket",
            "socket.create_connection",
            "socket.getaddrinfo",
            "os.getenv",
            "os._Environ.__getitem__",
            "os._Environ.get",
            "os._Environ.__contains__",
        ):
            guard = patch(target, side_effect=AssertionError(
                f"T-01 forbids network/environment access: {target}"
            ))
            guard.start()
            self.addCleanup(guard.stop)

    def provider(self, **kwargs):
        from access_intake.providers.mock import MockProvider

        return MockProvider(**kwargs)

    def test_t01_saved_reply_and_call_recording_are_deterministic(self):
        expected_reply = json.loads(REPLY.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        expected_text = expected_reply["output"][0]["content"][0]["text"]
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(expected_text), EXPECTED_FACTS)
        for quote in EXPECTED_FACTS["supporting_quotes"]:
            self.assertIn(quote, self.message)

        provider = self.provider(responses={"IT-001.json": REPLY})
        for _ in range(2):
            self.assertEqual(
                provider.extract("IT-001.json", self.message), expected_reply
            )
        self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [
            ("IT-001.json", self.message), ("IT-001.json", self.message)
        ])

    def test_t01_selected_error_is_raised_and_recorded(self):
        failure = ProviderUnavailable("T-01 injected provider failure")
        provider = self.provider(responses={"IT-001.json": failure})
        with self.assertRaises(ProviderUnavailable) as caught:
            provider.extract("IT-001.json", self.message)
        self.assertIs(caught.exception, failure)
        self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [("IT-001.json", self.message)])

    def test_t01_delayed_reply_waits_without_blocking_another_call(self):
        release = ObservedEvent()
        provider = self.provider(
            responses={"delayed": REPLY, "ready": REPLY},
            release_events={"delayed": release},
        )
        expected_reply = json.loads(REPLY.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        # Aliases select the same source fixture; they are not document-ID claims.
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as executor:
            pending = executor.submit(provider.extract, "delayed", self.message)
            try:
                self.assertTrue(release.waiting.wait(timeout=2), "no delay barrier")
                self.assertFalse(pending.done())
                self.assertEqual(
                    provider.extract("ready", self.message), expected_reply
                )
            finally:
                release.set()
            self.assertEqual(pending.result(timeout=2), expected_reply)
        self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [
            ("delayed", self.message), ("ready", self.message)
        ])

    def test_t01_offline_guards_are_active(self):
        # Verify guards themselves without inspecting the host environment.
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, "forbids network"):
            socket.create_connection(("example.invalid", 443))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, "forbids network/environment"):
            os.environ.get("T01_FORBIDDEN_ENVIRONMENT_LOOKUP")
        provider = self.provider(responses={"IT-001.json": REPLY})
        self.assertEqual(
            provider.extract("IT-001.json", self.message),
            json.loads(REPLY.read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
        )

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check that this computer and this copy of the repository are ready for the Challenge.

Run it from the root of your clone:

    python3 tools/check_prerequisites.py

It checks four things and prints PASS or FAIL for each, with what to do on a FAIL:

  1. Codex is installed and signed in.
  2. This folder is a clone of the Challenge repository, with every supplied file in place.
  3. Entire records your coding sessions in this repository.
  4. The repository's tests run on mock responses: no model is called and API_KEY is not used.

The last line is READY when all four pass. Python 3.10 or later, standard library only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SUPPLIED = ["CHALLENGE.md", "snapshot.schema.json", "materials/office-policy.md", "docs/requirements.md"]
REQUESTS = 20


def run(command: list[str], env: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300,
                          stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)


def check_codex() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    if not shutil.which("codex"):
        return False, "codex is not on your PATH. Install the Codex CLI the way the facilitator shows you, then open a new terminal."
    version = run(["codex", "--version"])
    if version.returncode != 0:
        return False, f"codex --version failed: {version.stderr.strip() or version.stdout.strip()}"
    login = run(["codex", "login", "status"])
    if login.returncode != 0:
        return False, f"{version.stdout.strip()} is installed but not signed in. Sign in with the class key the facilitator gives you."
    return True, f"{version.stdout.strip()}; {login.stdout.strip() or login.stderr.strip()}"


def check_clone() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    inside = run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"])
    if inside.returncode != 0 or Path(inside.stdout.strip()).resolve() != ROOT:
        return False, "this folder is not the top of a Git clone. Clone your copy of the repository and run this from its root."
    if not run(["git", "remote", "get-url", "origin"]).stdout.strip():
        return False, "the clone has no remote named origin. Clone your copy of the repository from GitHub."
    missing = [name for name in SUPPLIED if not (ROOT / name).is_file()]
    if missing:
        return False, f"missing supplied files: {', '.join(missing)}. Clone the repository again."
    exports = sorted((ROOT / "materials" / "requests").glob("*.json"))
    if len(exports) != REQUESTS:
        return False, f"materials/requests/ holds {len(exports)} JSON files, not {REQUESTS}. Clone the repository again."
    for path in exports:
        try:
            if not isinstance(json.loads(path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")).get("message"), str):
                return False, f"{path.name} has no message text. Clone the repository again."
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            return False, f"{path.name} is not UTF-8 JSON. Clone the repository again."
    return True, f"clone of {run(['git', 'remote', 'get-url', 'origin']).stdout.strip()}; {len(exports)} request exports read"


def check_capture() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    if not shutil.which("entire"):
        return False, "entire is not on your PATH. Install the Entire CLI as the course's session-capture guide says."
    status = run(["entire", "status", "--json"])
    try:
        state = json.loads(status.stdout)
    except ValueError:
        return False, f"entire status gave no answer: {status.stderr.strip() or status.stdout.strip()}"
    if not state.get("enabled"):
        return False, "Entire is not enabled in this repository. Run: entire enable --agent codex"
    if "Codex" not in (state.get("agents") or []):
        return False, "Entire is enabled but not for Codex. Run: entire agent add codex"
    return True, f"Entire enabled for {', '.join(state['agents'])}"


def check_tests() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if key != "API_KEY"}
    tests = run([sys.executable, "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests"], env=env)
    summary = [line for line in tests.stderr.splitlines() if line.startswith(("Ran ", "OK", "FAILED"))]
    if tests.returncode != 0:
        return False, "the tests failed with API_KEY unset:\n" + tests.stderr.strip()
    return True, "; ".join(summary) + " (API_KEY unset)"


def main() -> int:
    if sys.version_info < (3, 10):
        print(f"FAIL  Python {sys.version.split()[0]}: this Challenge needs Python 3.10 or later.")
        return 1
    checks = [("Codex", check_codex), ("Repository", check_clone),
              ("Session capture", check_capture), ("Tests on mock responses", check_tests)]
    passed = 0
    for number, (name, check) in enumerate(checks, 1):
        ok, detail = check()
        passed += ok
        print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {number}. {name}: {detail}")
    if passed == len(checks):
        print(f"READY: all {len(checks)} checks passed. Start docs/01-research-to-spec.md.")
        return 0
    print(f"NOT READY: {len(checks) - passed} of {len(checks)} checks failed. Fix each FAIL above and run this again;"
          " if one still fails, ask the facilitator.")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Build plan — IT access-request intake

This is a plan, not an implementation or a report of passing checks. Only planning/plan.md is updated in this task. All source files, fixtures, test names, commands and deliverables described below are planned work. The 89 requirements and 69 research questions in planning/spec.md remain unchanged. A planned test demonstrates only the behavior it actually exercises; mocked extraction does not establish live model accuracy.

## Choices

- **Runtime:** Python 3.10 or later, following the classroom prerequisite and existing unittest starter; the exact supported Python release and dependency versions will be pinned during implementation.
- **Interface:** a CLI using the prospective entry point `python3 -m access_intake`, because operators need intake, queue inspection, retry and resume without a required web deployment.
- **Test command:** `env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, matching the starter; tests use injected fake configuration, saved responses and controlled clocks/events, never a real key or live network.
- **Provider invocation:** OpenAI, as selected by the person in this session, through the Responses API over an injectable HTTP transport; build the deterministic fixture provider first. Use structured extraction output and exercise the real adapter through fake HTTP responses. The supported model and its settings remain G1.
- **State:** use a transactional store for document revisions, processing attempts and current-result references; select its backend and supported host topology at G2 before implementing concurrency guarantees.
- **Output:** current extraction JSONL and queue JSON are exports of one consistent recorded generation; history is stored separately and linked to its earlier attempt/source. Container details, pending-state presentation and failure provenance await G5.
- **Schema and fixtures:** keep the supplied extraction schema as the contract; choose a compatible validator and lockfile at G3. Hand-author expectations from the evidence catalogue below before writing response fixtures or measuring extraction outputs.

The selected API is grounded in the official [OpenAI Responses create reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/create) and [Structured Outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs), checked on 2026-11-13. Plan POST /v1/responses with a configured model and the extraction schema in text.format using json_schema. The non-streaming adapter checks response status, error and incomplete_details before parsing output_text content; a refusal content item is handled separately. Fake envelopes exercise completed output, refusal and incomplete status. Local schema and exact-quote validation still run after provider output is decoded. The model must support the chosen structured-output configuration; no model is inferred from documentation examples.

Implementation gates and questions for review follow the skill's instruction: “Where a spec line is unclear, say so in the plan and ask the person; do not guess a rule.” These are unresolved questions, not additions to the requirements. The person selected OpenAI after being asked about provider/model, source ordering and accuracy counting; the model, ordering and counting answers remain open.

| Gate | Question to resolve before dependent implementation | Related spec research and affected work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G1 | Which OpenAI model and supported request settings should be documented? | Q-02, Q-38, Q-49, Q-58, Q-69; OpenAI and the Responses API envelope are selected/documented above. S3's model-specific request configuration and S10's supported-configuration evidence remain gated. Fake transport checks need no key. |
| G2 | Is shared state supported on one host or multiple hosts, and what ordering defines the latest processed source when attempts overlap? | Q-05–Q-07, Q-46; S5/S7 need a store/topology decision. The different-revision race in T-33 cannot have a winner expectation until ordering is chosen. |
| G3 | Which validator/dialect and packaging lockfile will be supported, and what are the decisions for invalid exports, empty/unsupported facts and date validation? | Q-12–Q-21, Q-24–Q-28, Q-48, Q-66–Q-67; S2/S3 can plan the stated schema and supplied examples, but must not invent additional rejection or normalization rules. F-17 now uses the explicit document-update purpose quoted in its message; broader applicability questions stay open. |
| G4 | Which fields enter exact-match accuracy, with what treatment of prose, nulls, arrays, errors and denominators? | Q-25, Q-52–Q-56; S9's score assertions and final accuracy report remain gated. There is no invented accuracy pass threshold. |
| G5 | How are pending attempts, errors, response_source on no-response failures, provenance and current exports represented, and which retry attempt/source/settings are selected? | Q-20, Q-37, Q-40–Q-45, Q-57, Q-69; S5/S6/S8 need these explicit contracts before their serialization and retry-selection tests are fixed. |

Any unresolved gate blocks only its dependent implementation or assertion. It does not justify changing the spec, inserting guessed business rules, choosing a source-race winner, or reporting unverified coverage as complete. The remaining open questions stay in planning/spec.md for review; the plan addresses the supplied unambiguous cases without claiming to settle them all.

## Steps, in build order

For every step, first write its named tests, run them with API_KEY unset, and record the real failure before implementing that step. If a new test already passes, record that fact and do not manufacture a failure. Only then implement the step and run its tests and the whole suite. Test ownership below is exclusive: later steps run earlier tests for regression but do not claim to introduce them. A failing regression stops progression. ### Source-derived expected facts

The following catalogue fixes concrete facts for the supplied examples before any measured output exists. Each F-01–F-20 row refers to that file's decoded message. Expected document_id is the input filename; expected source_sha256 is SHA-256 of its original bytes, independently recomputed from the test input. Every record has the 14 schema keys; all non-enum scalar values are strings or null and supporting_quotes/issues are string arrays.

For each catalogue row, the quoted purpose span is a source-grounded fixture value for business_purpose. It is not a claim that every other faithful prose rendering is wrong; the scoring treatment remains G4. Identity/team, kind, system, environment, permission, dates and manager are anchored by the quoted evidence in that row. Planned supporting_quotes include the relevant exact source spans, with both alternatives mandatory for unresolved conflicts and the attempted instruction retained for overrides. Issues assertions concern the specified missing/conflicting/policy facts, not invented exact wording or array order. Unless a row identifies unresolved facts, no missing/conflicting fact is expected from the quoted complete request. Historical permission mentions do not create unresolved requested-permission conflicts.

### Planned command contract

These are prospective CLI forms for implementation and T-35/T-40, not commands executed in this planning task. S8 finalizes syntax and G5 settles retry/source selection before they become exact README commands. Use isolated writable paths for tests; no test modifies the supplied exports or uses the real model.

- Test suite: `env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.
- Intake: `env -u API_KEY python3 -m access_intake intake materials/requests --provider mock --fixtures tests/mock_responses --state <state-path> --output <output-directory>`.
- Queue: `env -u API_KEY python3 -m access_intake queue --state <state-path>`.
- Source/evidence/history inspection: `env -u API_KEY python3 -m access_intake show IT-001.json --state <state-path>`.
- Resume: `env -u API_KEY python3 -m access_intake resume --provider mock --fixtures tests/mock_responses --state <state-path> --output <output-directory>`.
- Retry: `env -u API_KEY python3 -m access_intake retry <document-id> --provider mock --fixtures tests/mock_responses --state <state-path> --output <output-directory>`; selection of the recorded source/settings and success-after-error behavior are G5.
- Accuracy: `env -u API_KEY python3 -m access_intake accuracy --expected <expected-data-path> --actual <extractions-path> --output <accuracy-report-path>`; comparison and denominator semantics are G4.

# Before block 1: check your setup

In class you work this Challenge in three blocks, each with its own file in this folder:

| Block | File | What you have at the end |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Research | `docs/01-research-to-spec.md` | `planning/spec.md`: the brief as numbered requirements, each with its check |

| 3. Implement, then validate | `docs/03-implement-and-validate.md` | the code and its tests, and `planning/validation.md`: each requirement met or not met, with evidence |

You do the work with Codex, a coding agent, inside this repository. Each file says what to ask
Codex for, what is on disk at the end, and how to tell it is right.

This file comes first. Four things must be true before block 1 starts, because each block builds on
them: Codex runs, you work in your own clone of the repository, Entire records your coding
sessions (the Challenge asks for that record with your code), and the tests run on mock responses
(saved model replies, so a test needs no model key and no network). Nobody starts block 1 until
the check below prints `READY`.

## Steps

1. **Get your own copy and clone it.** Use the copy of
   `https://github.com/GitRollTraining/ai-full-stack-it-access-requests` the facilitator assigned
   you, or fork it to your GitHub account. Then:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<your-account>/<your-repository>.git
   cd <your-repository>
   ```

   Run every command in these files from the root of that clone.

2. **Check Python.** `python3 --version` prints 3.10 or later.

3. **Check Codex.** `codex --version` prints a version, and `codex login status` says you are
   logged in. If not, sign in with the class key the facilitator gives you.

4. **Turn on session capture.** `entire version` prints a version (install the Entire CLI as the
   course's session-capture guide says, if it does not). Then, in the clone:

   ```bash
   entire enable --agent codex
   ```

   `entire status` now says Entire is enabled.

5. **Run the check.**

   ```bash
   python3 tools/check_prerequisites.py
   ```

## What is on disk at the end

Nothing new to commit except what `entire enable` adds (`.entire/` and `.codex/hooks.json`).
Commit those so your session record follows your code:

```bash
git add .entire .codex

```

## How to tell it is right

The check prints one line per check and ends with `READY`:

```text
PASS  1. Codex: ...
PASS  2. Repository: ...
PASS  3. Session capture: ...
PASS  4. Tests on mock responses: ...

```

A `FAIL` line says what to do. Fix it and run the check again. If a line still fails, ask the
facilitator before block 1 starts.
# Block 1. Research: the brief as a spec

The brief is written as prose, across four files. Before you plan or write code, turn it into a
**spec**: a list of numbered requirements, each one sentence a test or an inspection can check,
each with the words of the brief it comes from and how you will check it. Block 2 plans from the
spec, and block 3 checks what Codex built against it, line by line. A requirement missing from the
spec is one nobody will build or check.

Start only after `python3 tools/check_prerequisites.py` prints `READY`
(`docs/00-prerequisites.md`).

## What to read

| File | What it gives the spec |
|---|---|
| `CHALLENGE.md` | the task, and the files you submit, each with what it must contain |
| `docs/requirements.md` | the operating context, record and review behaviour, and § Verification: the cases your tests must cover |
| `materials/office-policy.md` | the fields to extract, the five review-queue rules in order, processing and recovery |
| `snapshot.schema.json` | the record each extraction must match |
| `materials/requests/` | the 20 message exports; read three or four to see what the rules meet |

## Steps

1. Start Codex in the root of your clone: `codex`.
2. Ask Codex to read the four files and draft `planning/spec.md`. Your request says:
   - one numbered requirement per line, `R-01`, `R-02`, ..., each one testable sentence;
   - for each, the file and section it comes from, with the exact words quoted;
   - for each, how it will be checked: which test, which file to inspect, or which command to run;
   - nothing invented: a requirement the files do not state is not in the spec.

   <details><summary>An example request, if you want a starting point</summary>

   ```text
   Read CHALLENGE.md, docs/requirements.md, materials/office-policy.md and snapshot.schema.json.
   Write planning/spec.md: a table with columns ID, Requirement, Source, Check. One row per
   requirement, IDs R-01 onward. Requirement is one sentence that a test or an inspection can
   check. Source names the file and section and quotes the exact words. Check says how we will
   know it is met: the test, the file to inspect, or the command. Do not add anything the files
   do not say. Do not write any code.
   ```

   </details>

3. Read the draft against the files yourself. Codex misses requirements and merges two into one
   line. Check that these each have their own lines:
   - every fact the policy says to extract, and the rules for missing, conflicting and corrected values;
   - each of the five review-queue rules, in the policy's order;
   - each processing and recovery rule: errors, retries, hashes, reruns, changed input, history;
   - each file `CHALLENGE.md` asks you to submit;
   - each case `docs/requirements.md` § Verification lists.
4. **Research what the text leaves unclear.** Ask Codex to list every place where two readings are
   possible, or where a term is not defined. For each, look it up (in the files first, then in the
   documentation of the tool or standard it names) and write what you found. Add a section
   `## Open questions` to the spec: each question, what you found, and what stays open. Do not turn
   an open question into a requirement by guessing.
5. Commit the spec:

   ```bash
   git add planning/spec.md
   git commit -m "Spec: the brief as numbered requirements"
   ```

## What is on disk at the end

`planning/spec.md`, committed: the requirements table, then `## Open questions`.

## How to tell it is right

- Every row quotes the words it comes from, and you found those words in the file it names.
- Every row's check could fail: "the code is correct" is not a check; "the test for IT-0nn gives
  status needs-information" is.
- Each case of `docs/requirements.md` § Verification and each of the five queue rules has its own row.
- `git log --oneline -1` shows the spec commit.

Codex's summary of what it wrote is not the check. Open `planning/spec.md` and read it.
# Block 2. Plan: build steps with the test plan inside

A plan turns the spec into ordered steps before any code exists, so you can see and fix a wrong
order or a missing step while it costs nothing. The **test plan** sits inside the plan: one row per
case your tests must cover, each with the input, the mock response the test uses in place of the
model, and the **expected facts**. You write the expected facts from the message and the office
policy, never from the program's output: a test whose expected values were copied from the output
passes whatever the program does.

Start from your committed `planning/spec.md` (`docs/01-research-to-spec.md`).

## The planning skill

This repository supplies a skill for this block: `.agents/skills/plan-from-spec/SKILL.md`. A skill
is a folder of instructions Codex loads when a task matches it. This one tells Codex what the plan
holds and how to check it. Read it once before you start; it is one page.

## Steps

1. Start Codex in the root of your clone and ask it to use the plan-from-spec skill on
   `planning/spec.md`. Ask for the plan only, no code.

   <details><summary>An example request</summary>

   ```text
   Use the plan-from-spec skill on planning/spec.md. Write planning/plan.md only; write no code
   and no tests yet.
   ```

   </details>

2. Read `planning/plan.md` and correct it, with Codex or by hand, until each of these holds:
   - Every spec line appears in § Coverage with a step that builds it and a test or check that shows
     it. A spec line Codex left out goes back in.
   - The test plan has its own row for each case of `docs/requirements.md` § Verification: a
     complete request, missing dates, conflicting details, embedded instructions, provider failure,
     an unchanged rerun, changed source content. Then the paraphrased request you author, a refusal
     or interrupted response, and a failed retry after a prior success.
   - Each row's input is a real export in `materials/requests/` (or the message you wrote), and you
     opened it and read the message.
   - Each expected fact quotes the message words and the policy rule it comes from. Work one row out
     yourself, from the message and the policy, before you accept Codex's version.
   - Each row's mock response is named: a saved reply under `tests/mock_responses/`, an error, or a
     cut-off reply. No test calls the real model, and none needs `API_KEY`.
   - The steps put the mock provider first, and each later step names the test written before it.
3. Commit the plan:

   ```bash
   git add planning/plan.md
   git commit -m "Plan: build steps and test plan"
   ```

## What is on disk at the end

`planning/plan.md`, committed, with four sections: Choices, Steps, Test plan, Coverage.

## How to tell it is right

- Count the spec's lines and the Coverage lines: the numbers match, or each missing line is under
  "Not yet covered" with its reason.
- Pick one test-plan row and check its expected facts against the message and the policy yourself.
  Every value has a quote beside it.
- `git log --oneline` shows the plan commit above the spec commit.
# Block 3. Implement, then validate against the spec

Codex now builds from your plan, one step at a time, each test written before the code it tests and
run on mock responses. Then you **validate**: you check what was built against the spec, line by
line, and mark each line met or not met, with evidence you can open or run again. Validation is
yours, not the agent's. Codex's summary of what it did is a claim about the code, not evidence: an
agent can report a step done that its tests never exercise.

Start from your committed `planning/plan.md` (`docs/02-plan-with-test-plan.md`).

## Part 1. Build, test first, on mock responses

1. Start Codex in the root of your clone and ask it to build `planning/plan.md` in its step order.
   Your request says:
   - for each step, first write the test the plan names, run it and show it failing, then stop;
     after you commit the failing test (`Test first: <step>`), write the code until it passes, then
     stop again so you commit it (`Step <n>: <step>`);
   - every test uses mock responses saved under `tests/mock_responses/`, and no test calls the real
     model or reads `API_KEY`;
   - the expected values in each test are the expected facts of the test plan, not values copied
     from a run;
   - after each step, run the whole test suite and stop if anything fails.
2. You make the commits: Codex's sandbox does not let it write to `.git`, and the commits are your
   record that each test failed before its code existed. If a step's new test already passes
   before any code is written, say so in its commit message (`Test first: <step> (already
   passes)`) rather than making it fail on purpose.
3. Watch the steps. After each one, run the tests yourself, with `API_KEY` unset:

   ```bash
   env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
   ```

   (If your plan chose another test command, use it, still with `API_KEY` unset, and write it in
   your README.)
4. When the steps are done, save the full test run and commit it with anything not yet committed:

   ```bash
   env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v > planning/test-run.txt 2>&1
   git add -A
   git commit -m "Build the plan's steps, tests first, on mock responses"
   ```

## Part 2. Validate each spec line

1. Create `planning/validation.md` with one row per line of `planning/spec.md`:

   | Spec line | Requirement | Met or not met | Evidence | Note |
   |---|---|---|---|---|

2. Fill each row yourself. You may ask Codex to point you to code or tests, but you open the
   evidence and you decide the mark:
   - **Evidence** is something a reviewer can open or run again: a test name and its line in
     `planning/test-run.txt`, a file and line in the code, or a command and what it printed.
   - A line is **met** only when its evidence shows the requirement. A test that passes but does not
     test this requirement is not evidence for it.
   - A line with no evidence, or evidence for only part of it, is **not met**, and the note says what
     is missing.
3. Under the table, write the count: how many lines are met, how many are not met.
4. Commit:

   ```bash
   git add planning/validation.md
   git commit -m "Validation: each spec line met or not met, with evidence"
   ```

## What is on disk at the end

- The code and its tests, the tests passing on mock responses.
- `planning/test-run.txt`: the saved run.
- `planning/validation.md`: every spec line marked met or not met, each with its evidence.

## How to tell it is right

- `planning/validation.md` has as many rows as `planning/spec.md`.
- Pick two rows marked met and open their evidence: each shows the requirement, not only a passing test.
- `env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` ends with `OK` on a fresh run.
- `git log --oneline` shows a `Test first:` commit before each step's code commit.

## After class, on your own

1. The spec lines marked not met: plan each, build it test first, and mark it again.
2. The review queue: run intake on the 20 exports and check each entry's status, owner and next
   action against the five rules of `materials/office-policy.md`, in order.
3. The accuracy check: compare the extracted fields with the expected facts you wrote from the
   messages, as `CHALLENGE.md` asks for `deliverables/accuracy.md`.
4. The rest of the files `CHALLENGE.md` § What to submit lists under `deliverables/`, and the README
   it asks for. Class time covers the spec, the plan, the build and its validation; these files
   finish the submission.

The facilitator supplies a model key through `API_KEY` for runs against the real model; the tests
never use it.

# Block 3. Implement, then validate against the spec

Codex now builds from your plan, one step at a time, each test written before the code it tests and
run on mock responses. Then you **validate**: you check what was built against the spec, line by
line, and mark each line met or not met, with evidence you can open or run again. Validation is
yours, not the agent's. Codex's summary of what it did is a claim about the code, not evidence: an
agent can report a step done that its tests never exercise.

Start from your committed `planning/plan.md` (`docs/02-plan-with-test-plan.md`).

## Part 1. Build, test first, on mock responses

1. Start Codex in the root of your clone and ask it to build `planning/plan.md` in its step order.
   Your request says:
   - for each step, first write the test the plan names, run it and show it failing, then stop;
     after you commit the failing test (`Test first: <step>`), write the code until it passes, then
     stop again so you commit it (`Step <n>: <step>`);
   - every test uses mock responses saved under `tests/mock_responses/`, and no test calls the real
     model or reads `API_KEY`;
   - the expected values in each test are the expected facts of the test plan, not values copied
     from a run;
   - after each step, run the whole test suite and stop if anything fails.
2. You make the commits: Codex's sandbox does not let it write to `.git`, and the commits are your
   record that each test failed before its code existed. If a step's new test already passes
   before any code is written, say so in its commit message (`Test first: <step> (already
   passes)`) rather than making it fail on purpose.
3. Watch the steps. After each one, run the tests yourself, with `API_KEY` unset:

   ```bash
   env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
   ```

   (If your plan chose another test command, use it, still with `API_KEY` unset, and write it in
   your README.)
4. When the steps are done, save the full test run and commit it with anything not yet committed:

   ```bash
   env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v > planning/test-run.txt 2>&1
   git add -A
   git commit -m "Build the plan's steps, tests first, on mock responses"
   ```

## Part 2. Validate each spec line

1. Create `planning/validation.md` with one row per line of `planning/spec.md`:

   | Spec line | Requirement | Met or not met | Evidence | Note |
   |---|---|---|---|---|

2. Fill each row yourself. You may ask Codex to point you to code or tests, but you open the
   evidence and you decide the mark:
   - **Evidence** is something a reviewer can open or run again: a test name and its line in
     `planning/test-run.txt`, a file and line in the code, or a command and what it printed.
   - A line is **met** only when its evidence shows the requirement. A test that passes but does not
     test this requirement is not evidence for it.
   - A line with no evidence, or evidence for only part of it, is **not met**, and the note says what
     is missing.
3. Under the table, write the count: how many lines are met, how many are not met.
4. Commit:

   ```bash
   git add planning/validation.md
   git commit -m "Validation: each spec line met or not met, with evidence"
   ```

## What is on disk at the end

- The code and its tests, the tests passing on mock responses.
- `planning/test-run.txt`: the saved run.
- `planning/validation.md`: every spec line marked met or not met, each with its evidence.

## How to tell it is right

- `planning/validation.md` has as many rows as `planning/spec.md`.
- Pick two rows marked met and open their evidence: each shows the requirement, not only a passing test.
- `env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` ends with `OK` on a fresh run.

"""SQLite single-host durable attempts with leases, fencing, and atomic exports."""
from contextlib import contextmanager
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3
import threading
import time
import uuid


def encoded(value):
    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)


class Store:
    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = Path(path).resolve()
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.changed = threading.Condition()
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL')
            db.executescript('''
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attempts (
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                    document_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL,
                    raw BLOB NOT NULL, settings TEXT NOT NULL, fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,
                    state TEXT NOT NULL, token TEXT, lease_until REAL,
                    record TEXT, created_at REAL NOT NULL, finished_at REAL);
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
                    document_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, latest INTEGER NOT NULL, current INTEGER);
                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS work ON attempts(state, lease_until);
            ''')

    @contextmanager
    def connection(self, write=False):
        db = sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=30)
        db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        try:
            db.execute('PRAGMA synchronous=FULL')
            if write:
                db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            yield db
            db.commit()
        except BaseException:
            db.rollback()
            raise
        finally:
            db.close()

    def register(self, document_id, raw, settings, force=False):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
        with self.connection(write=True) as db:
            latest = db.execute('SELECT a.* FROM documents d JOIN attempts a ON a.id=d.latest WHERE d.document_id=?', (document_id,)).fetchone()
            if not force and latest and latest['source_sha256']==digest and latest['fingerprint']==settings['fingerprint']:
                if latest['state'] in ('pending','running') or (latest['record'] and json.loads(latest['record'])['status']!='error'):
                    return latest['id']
            attempt_id = db.execute('INSERT INTO attempts(document_id,source_sha256,raw,settings,fingerprint,state,created_at) VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?)',
                (document_id,digest,raw,encoded(settings),settings['fingerprint'],'pending',time.time())).lastrowid
            db.execute('INSERT INTO documents(document_id,latest) VALUES(?,?) ON CONFLICT(document_id) DO UPDATE SET latest=excluded.latest', (document_id,attempt_id))
            return attempt_id

    @staticmethod
    def job(row):
        result = dict(row)
        result['settings'] = json.loads(result['settings'])
        result['record'] = json.loads(result['record']) if result['record'] else None
        return result

    def retry(self, document_id):
        with self.connection() as db:
            row = db.execute('SELECT a.* FROM documents d JOIN attempts a ON a.id=d.latest WHERE d.document_id=?',(document_id,)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise ValueError('unknown document; inspect queue for a document_id')
        return self.register(document_id, row['raw'], json.loads(row['settings']), force=True)

    def claim(self, now=None, lease_seconds=300):
        now = time.time() if now is None else now
        with self.connection(write=True) as db:
            row = db.execute("SELECT * FROM attempts WHERE state='pending' OR (state='running' AND lease_until<=?) ORDER BY id LIMIT 1",(now,)).fetchone()
            if row is None:
                return None
            token = uuid.uuid4().hex
            db.execute("UPDATE attempts SET state='running',token=?,lease_until=? WHERE id=?",(token,now+lease_seconds,row['id']))
            result = self.job(row)
            result.update(state='running',token=token,lease_until=now+lease_seconds)
            return result

    def renew(self, job, lease_seconds=300):
        with self.connection(write=True) as db:
            return db.execute("UPDATE attempts SET lease_until=? WHERE id=? AND token=? AND state='running'",
                (time.time()+lease_seconds,job['id'],job['token'])).rowcount == 1

    def finish(self, job, record):
        with self.connection(write=True) as db:
            changed = db.execute("UPDATE attempts SET state='completed',record=?,finished_at=?,lease_until=NULL WHERE id=? AND token=? AND state='running'",
                (encoded(record),time.time(),job['id'],job['token'])).rowcount
            if not changed:
                return False
            db.execute('UPDATE documents SET current=? WHERE document_id=? AND latest=?',(job['id'],job['document_id'],job['id']))
        with self.changed:
            self.changed.notify_all()
        return True

    def wait_for_completed(self, document_id, timeout=5):
        deadline = time.monotonic()+timeout
        with self.changed:
            while time.monotonic()<deadline:
                if any(r['document_id']==document_id for r in self.snapshot()['records']):
                    return True
                self.changed.wait(max(0,deadline-time.monotonic()))
        return False

    def snapshot(self):
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.execute('BEGIN')
            records = [json.loads(r[0]) for r in db.execute('SELECT a.record FROM documents d JOIN attempts a ON a.id=d.current ORDER BY d.document_id')]
            pending = [dict(id=r['id'],document_id=r['document_id'],source_sha256=r['source_sha256'],state=r['state'],lease_until=r['lease_until'],settings=json.loads(r['settings']))
                for r in db.execute("SELECT * FROM attempts WHERE state!='completed' ORDER BY id")]
        return {'records':records,'pending':pending}

    def history(self, document_id=None):
        with self.connection() as db:
            query = 'SELECT * FROM attempts'
            params = ()
            if document_id is not None:
                query += ' WHERE document_id=?'; params=(document_id,)
            rows = db.execute(query+' ORDER BY id',params).fetchall()
        return [dict(attempt_id=r['id'],document_id=r['document_id'],source_sha256=r['source_sha256'],
                     settings=json.loads(r['settings']),state=r['state'],created_at=r['created_at'],
                     finished_at=r['finished_at'],record=json.loads(r['record']) if r['record'] else None,
                     source_utf8=bytes(r['raw']).decode('utf-8',errors='replace')) for r in rows]

    def export(self, output):
        """Publish immutable files via one atomic current symlink; pin it when reading a pair."""
        output=Path(output).resolve();output.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        with (output/'.export.lock').open('a') as lock:
            fcntl.flock(lock,fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            # One DB read transaction for all export contents, including history.
            with self.connection() as db:
                db.execute('BEGIN')
                rows=db.execute('SELECT * FROM attempts ORDER BY id').fetchall()
                current={r[0] for r in db.execute('SELECT current FROM documents WHERE current IS NOT NULL')}
                records=[json.loads(r['record']) for r in rows if r['id'] in current]
                records.sort(key=lambda r:r['document_id'])
                history=[dict(attempt_id=r['id'],document_id=r['document_id'],source_sha256=r['source_sha256'],settings=json.loads(r['settings']),state=r['state'],record=json.loads(r['record']) if r['record'] else None) for r in rows if r['id'] not in current]
            generation=output/'generations'/uuid.uuid4().hex;generation.mkdir(parents=True)
            queue=[{k:r[k] for k in ('document_id','source_sha256','attempt_id','status','owner','next_action','error','response_source')} for r in records]
            contents={'extractions.jsonl':''.join(encoded(r)+'\n' for r in records),
                      'queue.json':json.dumps(queue,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)+'\n',
                      'history.jsonl':''.join(encoded(r)+'\n' for r in history)}
            for name,content in contents.items():
                with (generation/name).open('w',encoding='utf-8') as file:
                    file.write(content);file.flush();os.fsync(file.fileno())
            self._sync_directory(generation)
            self._sync_directory(generation.parent)
            temporary=output/('.current-'+uuid.uuid4().hex)
            temporary.symlink_to(generation.relative_to(output),target_is_directory=True)
            os.replace(temporary,output/'current')
            for name in contents:
                target=output/name
                if not target.is_symlink():
                    temp=output/('.link-'+uuid.uuid4().hex);temp.symlink_to(Path('current')/name);os.replace(temp,target)
            self._sync_directory(output)
            return generation

    @staticmethod
    def _sync_directory(path):
        fd=os.open(path,os.O_RDONLY|os.O_DIRECTORY)
        try:os.fsync(fd)
        finally:os.close(fd)

"""Bounded independent workers; recorded source/settings drive retries and recovery."""
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shlex
import threading

from access_intake.policy import route
from access_intake.prompt import PROMPT
from access_intake.providers.mock import MockProvider
from access_intake.providers.openai import OpenAIProvider, ProviderError
from access_intake.validation import ROOT, SCHEMA, decode_export, extract_response


def settings_for(provider='mock', model='gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14', fixtures=ROOT/'tests/mock_responses',
                 policy=ROOT/'materials/office-policy.md', temperature=0, max_output_tokens=2400,
                 timeout=60, endpoint='https://api.openai.com/v1/responses'):
    if provider not in ('mock','openai'):
        raise ValueError('provider must be mock or openai')
    if timeout <= 0 or max_output_tokens < 1 or not 0 <= temperature <= 2:
        raise ValueError('invalid timeout, token limit or temperature')
    # Restrict credentials to the supported HTTPS provider; no arbitrary credential destination.
    if endpoint != 'https://api.openai.com/v1/responses':
        raise ValueError('only the OpenAI HTTPS Responses endpoint is supported')
    policy_text=Path(policy).read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    settings=dict(provider=provider,model=model,temperature=temperature,max_output_tokens=max_output_tokens,
                  timeout=timeout,endpoint=endpoint,policy_text=policy_text,
                  policy_sha256=hashlib.sha256(Path(policy).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                  schema_sha256=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(SCHEMA,sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest(),
                  prompt_sha256=hashlib.sha256(PROMPT.encode()).hexdigest(),
                  implementation_sha256=hashlib.sha256(b''.join(p.read_bytes() for p in sorted((ROOT/'access_intake').rglob('*.py')))).hexdigest())
    if provider=='mock':
        settings['fixtures']=str(Path(fixtures).resolve())
        settings['fixtures_sha256']=hashlib.sha256((Path(fixtures)/'corpus-completed.json').read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    settings['fingerprint']=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(settings,sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
    return settings


class Engine:
    def __init__(self, store, provider=None, settings=None):
        self.store=store;self.provider=provider;self.settings=settings

    def enroll(self, paths):
        if self.settings is None:
            raise ValueError('intake requires processing settings')
        return [self.store.register(Path(path).name,Path(path).read_bytes(),self.settings) for path in paths]

    def retry(self, document_id):
        return self.store.retry(document_id)

    def run(self, workers=4):
        if workers < 1 or workers > 32:
            raise ValueError('workers must be 1..32')
        def worker():
            while True:
                job=self.store.claim()
                if job is None:return
                stopped=threading.Event()
                def heartbeat():
                    while not stopped.wait(60):
                        if not self.store.renew(job):return
                thread=threading.Thread(target=heartbeat,daemon=True);thread.start()
                try:
                    record=self.process(job)
                    self.store.finish(job,record)
                finally:
                    stopped.set();thread.join()
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
            # Resolve every worker so persistence failures are surfaced to the operator.
            futures=[pool.submit(worker) for _ in range(workers)]
            for future in futures:future.result()

    def process(self, job):
        settings=job['settings'];provider=self.provider
        source='mock' if settings['provider']=='mock' else 'openai:'+settings['model']
        record=dict(document_id=job['document_id'],source_sha256=job['source_sha256'],
                    attempt_id=job['id'],response_source=source,provenance=settings,
                    extraction=None,error=None)
        try:
            try:
                export=decode_export(job['raw'])
            except (ValueError,UnicodeError):
                raise ValueError('invalid UTF-8 JSON export; message string required') from None
            if provider is None:
                provider=MockProvider(fixtures=settings['fixtures']) if settings['provider']=='mock' else OpenAIProvider(settings)
            reply=provider.extract(job['document_id'],export['message'])
            f=extract_response(reply,export['message'])
            routing,f=route(f,job['document_id'],export['message'])
            record.update(routing,extraction=f)
            if settings['provider']=='openai':
                record['response_source']='openai:'+ (getattr(provider,'response_model',None) or settings['model'])
        except Exception as exc:
            # Only controlled local messages are exposed; arbitrary adapter/HTTP body text is discarded.
            safe=str(exc) if isinstance(exc,ProviderError) else 'extraction validation failed' if isinstance(exc,ValueError) else 'provider failure'
            # Validation messages are controlled by our validator; use fixed category instead of raw JSON/body.
            if isinstance(exc,ValueError):
                known=('refusal','interrupted','incomplete','malformed','quote','export','schema','properties','date','output')
                safe=next((f'{word}: extraction validation failed' for word in known if word in str(exc)),safe)
            retry=shlex.join(['python3','-m','access_intake','retry',job['document_id'],'--state',str(self.store.path)])
            record.update(status='error',owner='IT Service Desk',next_action='retry-extraction',extraction=None,
                error={'category':'provider' if not isinstance(exc,ValueError) else 'validation','message':safe,'retry_command':retry})
        return record

"""Field comparisons against the independent source/policy oracle."""
import json
from access_intake.validation import SCHEMA


def compare(expected, actual):
    indexed={}
    for record in actual:
        key=record['document_id']
        if key in indexed:
            raise ValueError('duplicate document_id in actual results')
        indexed[key]=record
    fields=list(SCHEMA['properties'])
    matched=0;route_matched=0;errors=[];failed=0
    for name,oracle in expected.items():
        record=indexed.get(name)
        extraction=record.get('extraction') if record else None
        if not isinstance(extraction,dict):failed+=1
        for key in fields:
            want=oracle['extraction'][key]
            present=isinstance(extraction,dict) and key in extraction
            got=extraction.get(key) if isinstance(extraction,dict) else None
            if present and type(got) is type(want) and got==want:
                matched+=1
            else:
                errors.append(dict(document_id=name,field=key,expected=want,actual=got,
                    category='processing-failure-or-missing' if not isinstance(extraction,dict) else
                             'omission' if got is None and want is not None else
                             'unsupported-fact' if want is None and got is not None else
                             'evidence-or-issue-difference' if key in ('issues','supporting_quotes') else 'different-value'))
        for key,want in oracle['route'].items():
            if record and record.get(key)==want:route_matched+=1
    return dict(matched=matched,denominator=len(expected)*len(fields),routing_matched=route_matched,
                routing_denominator=len(expected)*3,failed_or_missing=failed,factual_errors=errors,
                unexpected_documents=sorted(set(indexed)-set(expected)),
                response_sources=sorted({str(r.get('response_source')) for r in actual}),
                configurations=[json.loads(v) for v in sorted({json.dumps(r.get('provenance',{}),sort_keys=True) for r in actual})])


def markdown(expected,actual):
    report=compare(expected,actual)
    lines=['# Accuracy comparison','',
        'Observation: saved mock responses exercise the pipeline; this is not measured live model accuracy. '
        'No live model call was made for the submitted bundle. For a provider replay, the response_sources and configurations below identify the actual producers.', '',
        'Oracle: tests/expected.json, transcribed before production code from planning/plan.md F-01–F-21. '
        'Each source is independently readable; whole-message evidence retains both conflict alternatives. '
        'Absence expectations require reading the entire message. Policy rules 1–5 determine the route.', '',
        'Procedure: join by document_id. Compare all 14 schema fields with exact JSON equality, including '
        'case, punctuation, whitespace, null and array ordering/duplicates. No prose normalization. '
        'Null equals null. Missing fields never match null. Each of 21 expected documents contributes '
        '14 slots (294 total), including failures or absent records, which score zero for all 14 fields. '
        'Extra documents are reported separately; duplicates reject the comparison. '
        'Routes are counted separately: three slots per document (63). No minimum pass threshold is imposed.', '',
        'Factual-error reporting includes omissions, unsupported values, differing values, evidence/issue '
        'differences and processing failures. Literal purpose/issue wording differences can be faithful '
        'paraphrases rather than factual mistakes; inspect each reported difference against source.', '',
        f"Observed field matches: {report['matched']}/{report['denominator']}",
        f"Observed route matches: {report['routing_matched']}/{report['routing_denominator']}",
        f"Failed or missing documents: {report['failed_or_missing']}", '',
        'Configuration and response source:', '```json',json.dumps({k:report[k] for k in ('response_sources','configurations')},indent=2),'```','',
        'Expected fields (independent source oracle; not measured outputs):','']
    for name,oracle in expected.items():
        lines += [f"## {name} — {oracle['source']}",'',oracle['oracle'],'','```json',json.dumps(oracle,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2),'```','']
    lines+=['Comparison differences / factual-error candidates:','', '```json',json.dumps(report['factual_errors'],ensure_ascii=False,indent=2),'```','',
            'Unexpected documents: '+json.dumps(report['unexpected_documents']), '']
    return '\n'.join(lines),report

cat > access_intake/__main__.py <<'PY'
"""Documented CLI: intake, queue, show, retry, resume, export, accuracy."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

from access_intake.accuracy import markdown
from access_intake.engine import Engine, settings_for
from access_intake.store import Store
from access_intake.validation import ROOT


def parser():
    result=argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Prepare access requests for human review')
    commands=result.add_subparsers(dest='command',required=True)
    for name in ('intake','queue','show','retry','resume','export'):
        command=commands.add_parser(name)
        command.add_argument('--state',type=Path,default=Path('.state/intake.sqlite'))
        if name in ('intake','retry','resume','export'):
            command.add_argument('--output',type=Path,default=Path('deliverables'))
        if name in ('intake','retry','resume'):
            command.add_argument('--workers',type=int,default=4)
        if name in ('show','retry'):
            command.add_argument('document_id')
        if name=='intake':
            command.add_argument('inputs',type=Path)
            command.add_argument('--provider',choices=('mock','openai'),default='mock')
            command.add_argument('--fixtures',type=Path,default=ROOT/'tests/mock_responses')
            command.add_argument('--model',default='gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14')
            command.add_argument('--temperature',type=float,default=0)
            command.add_argument('--max-output-tokens',type=int,default=2400)
            command.add_argument('--timeout',type=float,default=60)
            command.add_argument('--policy',type=Path,default=ROOT/'materials/office-policy.md')
    accuracy=commands.add_parser('accuracy')
    accuracy.add_argument('--expected',type=Path,required=True)
    accuracy.add_argument('--actual',type=Path,required=True)
    accuracy.add_argument('--output',type=Path,required=True)
    return result


def main(argv=None):
    args=parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        if args.command=='accuracy':
            expected=json.loads(args.expected.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
            actual=[json.loads(line) for line in args.actual.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines() if line.strip()]
            text,report=markdown(expected,actual)
            args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            args.output.write_text(text,encoding='utf-8')
            print(json.dumps({k:report[k] for k in ('matched','denominator','routing_matched','routing_denominator','failed_or_missing')}))
            return 0 if report['matched']==report['denominator'] and report['routing_matched']==report['routing_denominator'] and not report['unexpected_documents'] else 1
        if args.command in ('queue','show') and not args.state.is_file():
            raise ValueError('state database does not exist; start intake first')
        store=Store(args.state)
        engine=Engine(store)
        if args.command=='queue':
            print(json.dumps(store.snapshot(),ensure_ascii=False,indent=2));return 0
        if args.command=='show':
            history=store.history(args.document_id)
            if not history:raise ValueError('unknown document_id')
            print(json.dumps({'document_id':args.document_id,'history':history},ensure_ascii=False,indent=2));return 0
        if args.command=='intake':
            settings=settings_for(provider=args.provider,model=args.model,fixtures=args.fixtures,policy=args.policy,
                temperature=args.temperature,max_output_tokens=args.max_output_tokens,timeout=args.timeout)
            paths=sorted(args.inputs.glob('*.json')) if args.inputs.is_dir() else [args.inputs]
            if not paths:raise ValueError('input directory contains no JSON exports')
            engine=Engine(store,settings=settings)
            engine.enroll(paths)
        if args.command=='retry':engine.retry(args.document_id)
        if args.command in ('intake','retry','resume'):engine.run(args.workers)
        generation=store.export(args.output)
        print(json.dumps({'generation':str(generation),'records':len(store.snapshot()['records']),
                          'pending':len(store.snapshot()['pending'])}))
        return 0
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print('intake interrupted; completed records are durable; resume after lease expiry',file=sys.stderr)
        return 130
    except (ValueError,OSError) as exc:
        # No arbitrary input/provider body text or credentials in operational logs.
        print(f'{type(exc).__name__}: command could not complete; check input paths, arguments and state; use --help',file=sys.stderr)
        return 2


if __name__=='__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
